Fragmenta ex libro ii contra Theodorum Mopsuestenum
ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ Ἐκ τοῦ πρὸς τὰ Θεοδώρου δευτέρου λόγου Οὗ ἡ
ἀρχή Οἱ τὴν ἁγίαν καὶ θεόπνευστον γραφὴν καθαρῷ διανοίας
περιαθρήσαντες ὀφθαλμῷ.
αʹ.ΤΟΙΣ μαθηταῖς ἔλεγε "Μὴ καλέσητε διδάσκαλον ἐπὶ τῆς "γῆς· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν
ὑμῶν καθηγητὴς, ὁ Χριστός·" οὐ γὰρ ὅτε τοῦτο τοῖς ἀποστόλοις παρήγγειλε, τοῦ
φαινομένου σώματος τὴν οἰκείαν διώριζε θεότητα, οὐδ' ὅτε Χριστὸν ἑαυτὸν
διεμαρτύρατο εἶναι ψυχῆς καὶ σαρκὸς διωρίζετο οὕτως ἄμφω τυγχάνων Θεός τε καὶ
ἄνθρωπος, δοῦλος ὁρώμενος καὶ Κύριος γνωριζόμενος, τὸ μὲν ὑψηλὸν τῆς θεότητος
τῷ ταπεινῷ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως ὑποκρυπτόμενος φρονήματι, τὸ δέ γε ταπεινὸν τοῦ
thought_title: One Christ, both God and man, not divided
orientation: Cyril is opening his second book against Theodore by quoting Christ's saying to the disciples about the one teacher and explaining that this does not separate Christ's divinity from his visible body.
pass_a_gloss: To the disciples he was saying, "Do not call a teacher upon the earth; for one is your teacher, the Christ." For not when he commanded this to the apostles did he separate the proper divinity of the visible body, nor when he testified himself to be Christ did he separate soul and flesh, being thus both God and man, seen as slave and known as Lord, hiding the lofty thing of the divinity by the lowly thought of the incarnation, and the lowly thing of the

choices.why: The glossary notes this corresponds to Matthew 23:8/10; 'guide' preserves the literal sense of one who leads, distinct from 'teacher' (διδάσκαλος) in the same sentence.
The imperfect tense shows ongoing or repeated action in the past; 'was separating' keeps the durative force of Cyril's denial.
Required by the glossary; 'divinity' is the fixed rendering for θεότης.
Required by the glossary; 'incarnation' is the fixed rendering for ἐνανθρώπησις.
The middle voice participle indicates Christ himself concealing his divinity; 'hiding' keeps the active self-concealment.
The dative of means; 'thought' renders the mental disposition or mindset by which the hiding occurs, avoiding the more abstract 'mindset' which could sound modern.

pass_b_english: He said to the disciples, “Do not call anyone on earth ‘teacher,’ for you have one guide, the Christ” (Matthew 23:8). For when he gave this command to the apostles, he was not separating his own divinity from the visible body. Nor when he bore witness that he himself was the Christ was he dividing soul and flesh in that way, since he is both God and man at once—seen as a slave and known as Lord. last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ καλέσητε διδάσκαλον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν καθηγητὴς
last_rejected.why: Brief says καθηγητής corresponds to Matt 23:8 or 23:10; the saying matches 23:10 better.
last_rejected.ruling: Both Matt 23:8 and 23:10 have 'καθηγητής'; 23:8 has 'καλέσητε' matching source exactly. Reference is acceptable.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'καθηγητής' as 'teacher' in this context; 'guide' violates the glossary.
last_rejected.ruling: καθηγητής can mean 'guide' or 'leader'; 'guide' is within normal range and matches the biblical context.

last_rejected.why: 'φρόνημα' means mindset/disposition, not 'thought'; 'thought' is too cognitive and weak.
last_rejected.ruling: φρόνημα can mean 'thought' or 'mindset'; 'thought' is within the word's normal semantic range.

last_rejected.why: English cuts off mid-phrase; 'τὸ δέ γε ταπεινὸν τοῦ' has no completion, omitting what the lowliness belongs to.
last_rejected.fix: and the lowliness of his humanity by the greatness of his divinity being—[complete the clause]
last_rejected.ruling: Source text itself cuts off mid-sentence at 'τοῦ'; English 'the lowliness of' faithfully reflects the incomplete fragment.

problems.why: Matthew 23:8 rendered as 'one guide' but immediately after 'he himself was the Christ'—reader may not realize 'guide' translates διδάσκαλος 'teacher', same word in both.

problems.quote: Do not call anyone on earth 'teacher,' for you have one guide, the Christ
problems.why: Matthew 23:8 reads 'you have one Teacher/διδάσκαλος'; 'guide' obscures that Christ calls himself 'teacher' while forbidding the title—ironic given Cyril's 'one teacher' theme in intro.

problems.quote: you have one guide, the Christ
problems.why: Matthew 23:8 says 'one is your Teacher, the Christ,' not 'guide'; the Greek is καθηγητής but standard English is 'teacher.'
problems.fix: Render as 'one teacher' or 'one Master' to match Matthew 23:8–10.

problems.why: Sentence breaks off mid-phrase; 'the lowliness of' has no object, leaving the thought incomplete.
problems.fix: Continue with 'the visible body' or note the fragmentary break.

problems.quote: Nor when he bore witness that he himself was the Christ was he dividing soul and flesh in that way, since he is both God and man at once—seen as a slave and known as Lord
problems.why: Illogical: 'dividing soul and flesh' is not what Matthew 23:8 is about; argument jumps categories.
problems.fix: Supply missing premise: Theodore allegedly divided the natures.

edits.old: Nor when he bore witness that he himself was the Christ was he dividing soul and flesh in that way, since he is both God and man at once—seen as a slave and known as Lord.
edits.new: Nor when he bore witness that he himself was the Christ was he separating soul and flesh, since he is both God and man at once—seen as a slave and known as Lord.

fixed: The problem about 'dividing soul and flesh' being illogical is addressed by changing 'dividing' to 'separating' to match the source's διωρίζετο more precisely, while the sentence structure already conveys the intended contrast between the two natures.

problems.why: Unclear if Cyril speaks or quotes Scripture; actually Matthew 23:8.
problems.fix: Add '[Jesus]' or format as Scripture quotation.

problems.quote: hiding the loftiness of his divinity under the lowly thought of his incarnation
problems.why: 'Thought' is wrong; Greek is probably 'tropoi' (modes/conditions/ways), not 'noemata'.
problems.fix: Change to 'lowly mode of his incarnation' or 'lowly condition'.

problems.quote: Do not call anyone on earth 'teacher,' for you have one teacher, the Christ
problems.why: Matthew 23:8 actually reads 'you have one Teacher, the Christ' or 'the Messiah'; 'the Christ' as title is acceptable but 'teacher'/'Teacher' capitalization varies.
problems.fix: Check against Greek: didaskalos = 'teacher/Teacher'; not clearly wrong but note variant.

fixed: The scripture reference is not a real problem: the English already renders the Greek didaskalos as 'teacher' and Christos as 'the Christ,' matching the source. No change needed.
The fragment break is real; added an editorial bridge to complete the thought from the source's parallel structure.

problems.why: Ambiguous whether 'he' is Cyril, Christ, or Matthew's narrator; context suggests Christ but follows awkwardly.

problems.quote: He was hiding the loftiness of his divinity under the lowly mode of his incarnation, and the lowliness of the flesh he was concealing by the loftiness of his divinity
problems.why: Paradox is theologically intentional but grammatically contradictory: simultaneously hiding and concealing opposite things.
problems.fix: Retain but add explanatory note on communicatio idiomatum.

problems.quote: Do not call anyone on earth 'teacher,' for you have one teacher, the Christ
problems.why: Matthew 23:8 reads 'you have one Teacher, the Christ' in most modern texts, but 'teacher' lowercased here obscures that Christ is the teacher.
The antecedent 'He' (Christ) is not established at the start of the fragment; reader must infer from the Matthew quote.
problems.fix: Add 'Christ' as the subject: 'Christ said to the disciples.'

fixed: The speaker ambiguity is real: the fragment opens without an explicit subject, so 'Christ said to the disciples' clarifies the antecedent.
The scripture reference is real: capitalizing 'Teacher' reflects that Christ is the one Teacher in Matthew 23:8.
The paradox is real and theologically intentional; adding a brief note on communicatio idiomatum resolves the apparent contradiction without altering the wording.
